connections.why: Identifying long-run change is the basis for explaining its causes and judging its significance
Disputes over causation and significance are exactly what generate differing historical interpretations
Understanding rival interpretations precedes weighing their relative strength
The breadth study trains the long-span change analysis the themes paper extends
Close depth study reveals the development and turning points within the period
Tracing development supplies the evidence for a supported judgement
Evaluated primary evidence underpins the conclusions reached
Depth-study technique is reapplied to the in-depth aspects of the themes paper
Primary source evaluation skills transfer directly to the Paper 3 source enquiry
Aspects in depth illustrate and test the broad thematic claims
Detailed episodes provide the evidence synthesised into the final argument
Source enquiry feeds evaluated evidence into the argued response
Working with interpretations in Paper 1 directly prepares the historiographical core of the NEA
Evaluating interpretations is the central skill demanded by the coursework
Depth-study source evaluation models the evidence handling required in the NEA
Source enquiry practice supports the independent evaluation of evidence in coursework
A focused enquiry question frames which scholarly interpretations are relevant
Engaging with rival interpretations leads to a reasoned independent judgement
Evaluated evidence substantiates the final independent conclusion
Synthesising breadth and depth models the argued judgement the NEA requires
